To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light emission from discharge of catalyst supported DBD reactors was different possibly due to light absorption and scattering effect by catalyst layer, and the catalyst layer of Fe2O 3 has higher light absorption effect compared to TiO 2 and Al 2O 3.
the catalyst layer of Fe2O 3 has the highest light absorbance effect compared with TiO2 and alumina, and the catalyst-supported DBDs have the similar O3 generation properties.
catalyst layers of FeO2 and TiO2 have little effect on the plasma discharges and ozone generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a characterization of catalyst-supported DBD reactor for ozone generation and PM oxidation.
the development of the catalyst-supported dielectric barrier discharge (DB) reactor for PM oxidative removal.
the development of a catalyst-supported DBD reactor for PM removal, which can be used as a PM control device in indoor and outdoor environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
catalyst-supported DBD reactor can be used for the removal of particulate matters (PMs) from flue gases.
the catalyst-supported DBDs are effective for PM oxidation, and that the catalytic effect on PM oxidation is mainly due to the light absorption by catalysts.
the catalyst layers have no influence on plasma discharges and the light emission from discharge gap, but they do affect the chemical reactions driven in plasma discharges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fe2O3 is a good catalyst for the oxidation of PM, while TiO2 and alumina (Al2O3) do not have obvious catalytic effect on PM oxidation.
the DBD reactor with catalyst layer has a potential application for PM oxidative removal.
the catalyst layers do not obviously influence discharge properties and O3 generation, but the catalyst layers have a great influence on PM oxidative removal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DBD reactor with Fe2O2 catalyst layer has the highest ozone yield and light absorption effect, which can lead to higher efficiency of PM oxidative removal.
the catalyst layers do not obviously influence the plasma discharges and the generation of O3 in the DBD reactors.
the DBD reactor can be easily supported with catalysts for the PM removal and the catalysts do not significantly influence the discharge properties.
